Paragraph:
Translation: All men are forced to act helplessly according to the impulses born of the modes of material nature; therefore no one can refrain from doing something, not even for a moment.

Purport (Excerpt): ...it is the nature of the soul to be always active... The body is only a dead vehicle to be worked by the spirit soul... In contact with material energy, the spirit soul acquires material modes... therefore, sannyasa, or any purificatory process, is to help reach the ultimate goal of becoming Krsna conscious...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The illusion that absolute physical and mental silence/inaction is possible while living in a material body.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna reveals a fundamental law of human nature: action is unavoidable. Biological, psychological, and environmental forces (the Gunas) continuously compel everyone to act moment to moment.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna realizes that complete inaction is a delusion; the real question is how to direct inevitable activity constructively.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Inevitability of Action: Accepting that human consciousness and biology are inherently dynamic
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Compulsive Environmental Conditioning: Recognizing how the modes of nature (gunas) compel behavior
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Channeling Drive: Directing unavoidable behavioral energy toward healthy goals

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Gunas (The three modes of material nature: Sattva, Rajas, Tamas)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Consciousness is inherently active. As long as one is conditioned by the material modes (sattva, rajas, tamas), one is helplessly driven to act. Because total inaction is impossible, one must channel this natural activity into purificatory, god-centered work.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Human psychology and biology are built for motion; mental and physical stillness cannot be forced by suppressing activity. Because your internal drive and environmental conditioning will compel you to do *something*, health lies in actively choosing constructive, value-aligned behaviors rather than attempting impossible passivity.
